item.title: Harry Styles Covers Simon & Garfunkel and Reimagines Deep Cuts at Intimate Meltdown Festival Set in London
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our podcast, where we dive into the latest music news and trends. I'm your host, and today we're talking about Harry Styles' exciting performance at the Meltdown Festival in London.
[Soft music continues in the background]
Host: Fresh from opening his 12-night stand at Wembley Stadium, Harry Styles took the stage at the Royal Festival Hall for a special one-off show with the Jules Buckley Orchestra. This intimate performance was part of the Meltdown Festival, which Styles is curating this year, following in the footsteps of legends like David Bowie and Grace Jones.
[Short music transition]
Host: The 13-song setlist was a treat for fans, with Styles performing rarely-played songs like "Two Ghosts" from his debut album, and new arrangements of tracks from his latest album. He also covered songs by Patrick Watson and closed the show with a beautiful rendition of Simon & Garfunkel's "Bridge Over Troubled Water".
[Short music transition]
Host: Styles has been making waves with his Together, Together residency tour, which kicked off in Amsterdam and has now taken over Wembley Stadium for 12 nights. In fact, he's broken the record for the most shows by an artist in a calendar year at the historic venue, surpassing Coldplay's 10-show stand in 2025.
[Outro music starts playing]
Host: That's all for today's episode. Thanks for tuning in to our podcast, and we'll catch you in the next one. If you want to see the full setlist from Harry Styles' Meltdown Festival show, check out our show notes.
[Outro music continues to play until the end]
